access_continuity_justification: Not yet met. The repository is owned by the `presidio-v` organisation, PyPI publishing uses Trusted Publishing (no personal token), and the release signing key is in the organisation password manager. But one person (`vstantch`) is the only repository admin and the only required reviewer of the `release` environment; the second code owner (`ceoofcyber`) has write access but cannot approve a release, and an emergency-access arrangement is not documented in this repository. Without that person, releases could not be cut within a week. To meet it: add a second `release`-environment reviewer, and document in `GOVERNANCE.md#project-continuity` how the owner credentials and signing key are recovered (as presidio-evidence does).
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: A command-line tool and library with no graphical or end-user UI; output is plain text or JSON.
assurance_case_justification: URL: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md`. Threat table with out-of-scope assumptions, the five trust boundaries of `ARCHITECTURE.md#trust-boundaries`, the secure-design-principles argument and the common-weakness argument (CWE-mapped). It states that two internal review passes were done and that there has been no external review or security audit.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs the full suite on every push and PR on Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13 (Ubuntu) with the Parquet and parity extras installed, including end-to-end run-then-verify tests, re-release chains (`tests/test_history.py`), the committed signed sample release and the shipped pass/fail vectors (`tests/test_public_contract.py`), the detector parity test against presidio-hardened-x402, and the Atheris fuzz job. All are required checks on `main`.
build_justification: Standard PEP 517 build with the `hatchling` backend: `python -m build` (or `uv build`) rebuilds the sdist and wheel from source; `publish.yml` does exactly this.
build_non_recursive_justification: A single PEP 517 build; there is no make or subdirectory build.
build_preserve_debug_justification: No compiled artefacts; the wheel is pure Python (`py3-none-any`).
build_repeatable_justification: The release is bit-for-bit reproducible: rebuilding `v0.7.0` from the tagged source (`git archive v0.7.0`, `uv build --wheel --sdist`, macOS) on 2026-11-08 gave a wheel (`6b7c2749…5ee6`) and an sdist (`7be28dac…298b`) whose SHA-256 match the PyPI files exactly. The package is pure Python built by `hatchling` (`>=1.31,<2`); the release build installs `build` unpinned, so reproducing a later release assumes a compatible backend version.
build_standard_variables_justification: A pure-Python package built by `hatchling`; no compiler or linker is invoked.
bus_factor_justification: The project has one active maintainer; a second person reviews pull requests as a code owner but does not hold admin or release rights. Bus factor is 1 today.
coding_standards_enforced_justification: `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` run in CI on every PR, in the required check `lint`.
coding_standards_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#style` — ruff lint and format, configured in `pyproject.toml` (line length 100, target Python 3.11, rule sets listed).
contribution_justification: URL: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md` — documents the fork → branch → PR flow against `main`.
contribution_requirements_justification: URL: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#requirements-for-acceptable-contributions` — ruff style config, test and coverage policy, security-sensitive-change rules, dependency bar.
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The signature algorithm is a per-signer trust-store field (`alg`, presidio-evidence `trust-store@1`), and the pseudonym scheme is recorded in each record (`hmac-sha256-128/v1`), so a new algorithm is a new identifier rather than a silent change. The file-hash function (SHA-256) is fixed by `dataset-release@1`; replacing it would be a new format (`@2`) verified side by side with `@1` (`SEMVER.md`), not a runtime switch.
crypto_call_justification: Ed25519 signing, verification and key generation come from `presidio-evidence` (backed by `cryptography`); SHA-256 and HMAC from the Python standard library (`hashlib.sha256`, `hmac.new`); random keys from `secrets`. No primitive is re-implemented.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: No key is in the source tree (only public trust stores for the sample and the test vectors). Keys are files supplied at run time (`--sign-key`, `--pseudonym-key`); trust stores are supplied by the buyer, and a signer may list several public keys, so a signing key rotates without a new release (`docs/KEYS.md`, tested in `tests/test_history.py`). Rotating the pseudonym key is possible but changes every pseudonym, as documented.
crypto_keylength_justification: Ed25519 signing keys (about 128-bit security), SHA-256 digests, and a 256-bit pseudonym key from `deident keygen`, all above the NIST 2030 minimum of 112 bits; pseudonyms are HMAC-SHA256 output truncated to 128 bits. The tool does not enforce a minimum length on a pseudonym key the operator supplies from elsewhere.
crypto_pfs_justification: The project implements no key-agreement or network protocol and makes no network calls.
crypto_published_justification: SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) for file, policy and list hashes; Ed25519 (RFC 8032) for the release signature (presidio-evidence `evidence-ref@3`); HMAC-SHA256 (RFC 2104) for per-recipient pseudonym-key derivation and pseudonyms.
crypto_random_justification: `deident keygen` (`src/presidio_deident/cli.py`) makes the pseudonym key with `secrets.token_bytes(32)` and the Ed25519 signing key with `presidio_evidence.generate_ed25519_keypair()` (`cryptography`, OS CSPRNG). Ed25519 signing is deterministic and needs no nonce.
crypto_used_network_justification: The project makes no network calls.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No SHA-1 and no CBC mode; the project does no encryption. The unkeyed SHA-256 suppression-list format is guessable for low-entropy values; this is a documented limit (`SECURITY.md#known-limits`, ADR-0006), not a security function.
crypto_working_justification: No MD4, MD5, single DES, RC4 or Dual_EC_DRBG anywhere in the code.
dco_justification: Contributions must carry a DCO `Signed-off-by` line (`git commit -s`), documented at `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#licensing-and-developer-certificate-of-origin-dco`; checked in review (there is no automated DCO check). Inbound = outbound `MIT`. The two commits on `main` so far are by the maintainer for the copyright holder (PRESIDIO Group) and carry no sign-off line.
delivery_mitm_justification: Distributed over HTTPS from PyPI and GitHub. `publish.yml` publishes through PyPI Trusted Publishing (OIDC, no stored API token) after a required reviewer approves the `release` environment (deployable from `v*` tags only); PyPI files carry PEP 740 attestations.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash is fetched over plain HTTP. Release tags are SSH-signed and GitHub-verified; the wheel and sdist carry build-provenance attestations (`gh attestation verify`).
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot (pip, GitHub Actions) with security updates enabled; `pip-audit` on every push and PR (`ci.yml`, required check `audit`); OpenSSF Scorecard weekly.
description_good_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident#readme` — the README opens with what the project does (de-identify a dataset before licensing it to an AI developer, and sign a release record that the buyer verifies offline) and the problem it addresses (documenting what was removed, what remained, which opt-out and deletion lists were applied, and the declared rights, in counts and hashes only, without claiming the output is anonymous).
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/issues` — searchable, URL-addressable, open, no proprietary client.
documentation_achievements_justification: The README front page shows and links the OpenSSF Best Practices badge (project 16454) next to the OpenSSF Scorecard badge; the badge image renders the current level.
documentation_architecture_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md` — components (one row per module), the run and verify flows, and five trust boundaries.
documentation_basics_justification: README (Install, the five releaser commands, the one buyer command against the committed sample release, the policy format, quasi-identifier risk, re-releases, formats), `docs/SPEC.md` (record format and verification algorithm), `docs/KEYS.md` (keys, trust-store delivery, rotation), `docs/THREAT-MODEL.md`, `SEMVER.md`, and the decision records in `docs/adr/`.
documentation_current_justification: Docs are updated in the same PR as the code they describe (`CHANGELOG.md` per version, `SEMVER.md`, `docs/SPEC.md` whose key table a test keeps in step with the schema, ADRs, `PRESIDIO-REQ.md` delivery status), and the README, `SECURITY.md` and `SEMVER.md` describe the current 0.7 line.
documentation_interface_justification: The external interface is the `deident` CLI (subcommands, options, exit codes 0/1/2), the `dataset-release@1` record format with its schema `schemas/dataset-release.v1.json`, the `verify --json` result `verify-result@1` and the check names; specified in `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/docs/SPEC.md` and enumerated in `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/SEMVER.md`, with usage in the README. The Python modules are documented as not yet a public API.
documentation_quick_start_justification: README "Install" (`pip install presidio-deident`), "Releaser: five commands" (`inspect`, `policy-init`, `keygen`, `run`, `verify`) and "Buyer: one command", which verifies the committed signed sample release (`deident verify examples/sample-release --trust examples/sample-trust.json`).
documentation_roadmap_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident#roadmap` has a dated "Next 12 months (to November 2027)" section: the first design-partner release and `dataset-release@2`, moving the schema to presidio-evidence, the shared PII package, DROP composite lists, the recipient-risk statement after legal review, and an external review before 1.0.
documentation_security_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/SECURITY.md` (security properties, known limits, reporting, release verification), `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/docs/THREAT-MODEL.md` (what a record proves and does not, attacks it stops, residual risks), `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md`, `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/docs/KEYS.md`, `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md#trust-boundaries`, and the design rationale in `docs/adr/` (ADR-0001 to ADR-0011).
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Tests are assertion-based (pytest) and run without `-O`; the fuzz harnesses also run without `-O`, so their assertions are checked.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No unfixed medium+ findings. The seeded mutation tests found that edited unsigned envelope fields still verified; fixed in 0.3.1 before publication.
dynamic_analysis_justification: The automated suite exceeds 80% branch coverage (449 of 462 branches fully covered, 2026-11-08; branch coverage is part of the 90% gate) and runs on every PR and release commit through CI. Two Atheris coverage-guided harnesses run in CI on every push and PR (`ci.yml`, required check `fuzz`, 60 s each): `fuzz/fuzz_readers.py` drives arbitrary input through the CSV and JSONL readers and the policy parser, asserting that only `DeidentError` escapes; `fuzz/fuzz_verify.py` replaces a signed release's record with arbitrary bytes and asserts that `verify_release` never raises and passes only for the original record. Seeded mutation tests (`tests/test_mutation.py`) mutate releases, inputs and policies.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The project is pure Python, which is memory-safe; it ships no native code.
english_justification: All docs and issue handling in English.
enhancement_responses_justification: Met by the documented process. No enhancement request has been received yet.
external_dependencies_justification: Listed machine-readably in `pyproject.toml`: one runtime dependency (`presidio-evidence[crypto]>=0.5.1,<0.6`, which brings `cryptography`), and the `parquet` (`pyarrow`), `parity` and `dev` extras. There is no lockfile. A CycloneDX SBOM (`sbom.cdx.json`) is generated by `publish.yml` and attached to each GitHub release.
governance_justification: Maintainer-led, single-steward model documented at `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md`: ordinary changes decided on the PR, security-relevant changes (`verify.py`, `release.py`, `_detect.py`, `tables.py`, `policy.py`, `schemas/`, `docs/SPEC.md`, the sample release) need a written rationale and may not weaken a default, compatibility changes follow `SEMVER.md`, disagreements escalate to PRESIDIO Group.
hardening_justification: Key files are written `0600`, never overwritten, and refused if group- or world-readable; outputs are `0600` in a `0700` directory, written to `<out>.partial` and renamed only after signing; symlinks and oversized JSON are refused; detector patterns are linear-time; errors never echo values. Supply chain: SHA-pinned GitHub Actions with least-privilege `permissions:`, Trusted Publishing behind a reviewer-gated `release` environment limited to `v*` tags, branch protection on `main` (code-owner review, last-push approval, admins included, linear history, 8 required checks), secret scanning with push protection.
implement_secure_design_justification: Fail-safe defaults: an unknown policy key, an unmapped or missing column, input that cannot be written back faithfully, unjustified PII in a kept column or a leftover `.partial` stops the run; every verify check must pass and malformed input is a failed check. Complete mediation: every listed file is re-hashed on every verify; nothing is cached. Least privilege: no network, no hosted mode, no values in any output; files `0600` in a `0700` directory. Defence in depth: signature over the record, record over the files, unsigned envelope fields bound to the record, `history` binding releases into one chain. Economy of mechanism: Ed25519 and SHA-256 via `presidio-evidence`/`cryptography` and the stdlib, no bespoke crypto, one runtime dependency. See `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#3-secure-design-principles-applied`.
input_validation_justification: Input data, policies, lists and received releases are untrusted. `policy.py` rejects unknown keys, unmapped columns and PII in free text (bounded to 512 characters); `tables.py` refuses non-UTF-8, lone surrogates, `NaN`/`Infinity`, nested, binary and decimal values and malformed CSV, naming row and column but never the value; `verify.py` accepts only plain-basename file names, refuses symlinks, size-bounds JSON and matches identifiers and timestamps in full before use. See `ARCHITECTURE.md#trust-boundaries`.
installation_common_justification: `pip install presidio-deident` (or `pip install 'presidio-deident[parquet]'` for Parquet) from PyPI.
installation_development_quick_justifica: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#local-verification` — create a venv, `pip install -e ".[dev]"`, then the ruff and pytest commands.
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installed via pip; `DESTDIR`-style conventions do not apply.
interact_justification: Obtaining: README "Install" (`pip install presidio-deident`, PyPI). Feedback and contributing: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md` (bug reports and feature requests via `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/issues`, the PR flow); vulnerability reports: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/SECURITY.md`. GitHub shows both files next to the README.
interfaces_current_justification: Dependencies are kept current by Dependabot (pip, Actions) with security updates enabled; ruff's `UP` rules flag outdated Python idioms; no deprecated FLOSS interface is used where a current one exists.
internationalization_justification: No user-facing localizable UI; CLI messages are short English diagnostics for operators.
know_common_errors_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md` maps swapped or edited files, edited records and envelopes, cross-dataset replay, path traversal and symlinks, resource exhaustion and value leakage to controls (section 1), and CWE-22, CWE-400/1333, CWE-20, CWE-200/532, CWE-330, CWE-798 and CWE-345/354 to named countermeasures (section 4); `docs/THREAT-MODEL.md` states what a record does and does not prove.
know_secure_design_justification: The design is fail closed (an unknown policy key, an unmapped column, unwritable input or unjustified PII in a kept column stops the run; a release verifies only if every check passes), least privilege and least data (no network, no hosted mode, records carry counts and hashes, never values; outputs `0600` in a `0700` directory), complete mediation (every listed file re-hashed on every verify), defence in depth (signature over the record, record over the files, unsigned envelope fields bound to the record) and economy of mechanism (all cryptography from `presidio-evidence` and `cryptography`). Argued in `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#3-secure-design-principles-applied`. Two internal review passes were done during development; there has been no external review or security audit.
maintained_justification: Release 0.7.0 on 2026-11-08 (`https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/releases`, PyPI); PR #2 merged 2026-11-08; CI, CodeQL, Scorecard and Dependabot active.
maintenance_or_update_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions` states the supported line (0.7.x; 0.7.0 is the first published version). `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/SEMVER.md` gives the upgrade path: a record that verifies keeps verifying in later 0.x versions, every record format verifies for the life of the project, patch releases fix bugs and security defects only, and users pin a minor version and re-verify the committed sample after each upgrade.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: gitleaks 8.30.1 over the full history on 2026-11-08 (all refs of the working repository, including the pre-public development history: 21 commits): the 12 hits are all the keyword argument `pseudonym_key=ws.pseudo_key` in tests, i.e. false positives. The only key material in the tree is public: the trust stores `examples/sample-trust.json` and `src/presidio_deident/vectors/*trust.json`. GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled.
regression_tests_added50_justification: Policy requires a regression test with every bug fix. All fixes in the last 6 months were made before publication (0.2.0, 0.3.1 and 0.5.0 in `CHANGELOG.md`), and each carries a regression test in the public tree: the 0.2.0 and 0.5.0 review fixes in `tests/test_review_fixes.py` (e.g. `test_detector_is_linear_on_long_runs`, `test_record_fields_are_checked`, `test_parent_to_another_recipient_is_refused`), and the 0.3.1 envelope binding in `tests/test_mutation.py` and the shipped vector `src/presidio_deident/vectors/envelope-mismatch`. The PRs are in the private development repository and are not linkable.
release_notes_justification: URL: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md` — hand-written per version (Added / Changed / Fixed), not VCS log output.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerability (CVE, GHSA or similar) has been fixed in any release; no security advisory exists for this repository. Defects found by the two internal review passes before publication (for example the quadratic email pattern fixed in 0.2.0) are listed under "Fixed" in `CHANGELOG.md`.
repo_interim_justification: Every change lands through a pull request from a pushed branch (direct pushes to `main` are blocked by branch protection), e.g. PR #2; interim work is visible between versions.
report_responses_justification: Met by the documented process. The repository became public on 2026-11-08 and no bug report has been received yet; the issue tracker is empty.
roles_responsibilities_justification: Key roles (steward org, maintainer, security contact, release manager, contributor) documented at `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities`.
signed_releases_justification: The wheel and sdist carry GitHub build-provenance attestations (`gh attestation verify <file> --repo presidio-v/presidio-deident`, bundle attached as `provenance.intoto.jsonl`), PyPI files carry PEP 740 attestations from Trusted Publishing, and release tags are SSH-signed with the public key in `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/allowed_signers`. Documented at `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases-and-obtaining-public-signing-keys`. Checked for `v0.7.0` on 2026-11-08 (wheel and sdist attestations and the tag signature verify).
sites_https_justification: The repository (GitHub), the package (PyPI) and the project page `https://www.presidio-group.eu/dataset-release/` are all served over HTTPS. The project runs no hosted service.
sites_password_security_justification: The project runs no site that authenticates users and stores no passwords.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's Python security queries, Bandit, and ruff's `S` rules (injection, unsafe deserialization, weak hashes, insecure randomness, hard-coded secrets and similar) as required CI checks.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Findings are fixed before merge; CI blocks on ruff and Bandit findings, and there are no open code-scanning alerts.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL for Python with the `security-extended` queries (`.github/workflows/codeql.yml`, results in GitHub code scanning, required check `CodeQL Analyze (Python)`), Bandit over `src/` (required check `Bandit SAST`), and ruff with the `S` (flake8-bandit) rule set in CI.
static_analysis_often_justification: CodeQL runs on every push and PR to `main`, plus a weekly scheduled run; ruff and Bandit run on every push and PR.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions on every push to `main` and every PR (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): lint, the test suite with the coverage gate on Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13 (Ubuntu), `pip-audit`, and the Atheris fuzz job. All are required checks on `main`.
test_justification: 12 pytest modules under `tests/` (186 tests on 2026-11-08: policy and table readers, detector, release run, verify, history chains, risk and generalisation, Parquet, California DROP lists, CLI, seeded mutation tests, review regressions, and the public contract with the shipped test vectors and the signed sample release). Licensed with the project. How to run: `CONTRIBUTING.md#local-verification`.
test_most_justification: CI enforces at least 90% combined line and branch coverage (`--cov-branch --cov-fail-under=90` in `pyproject.toml` `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`). Measured 98.6% on 2026-11-08 (1,295 statements with 11 missed, 462 branches with 13 partial). `tests/test_public_contract.py` verifies the committed signed sample release end to end.
test_policy_justification: URL: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests` — changes that add or modify functionality ship with tests in the same PR; bug fixes ship with a regression test that fails before and passes after.
test_policy_mandated_justification: Formal written policy at `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests`: functionality changes ship with tests; bug fixes include a regression test that fails before the fix. Enforced in code-owner review and by the 90% line-and-branch coverage gate.
test_statement_coverage80_justification: CI gate: at least 90% combined line and branch coverage (`--cov-branch --cov-fail-under=90` in `pyproject.toml`, applied by every `test` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`). Statement coverage measured 99.2% on 2026-11-08 (11 of 1,295 statements missed).
tests_are_added_justification: Example (0.2.0, `CHANGELOG.md`): the first internal review found the email pattern quadratic on long runs of local-part characters; the fix (a lookbehind anchor) shipped with `tests/test_review_fixes.py::test_detector_is_linear_on_long_runs` in the same change. Likewise every 0.5.0 fix from the second review has a test in that file (e.g. `test_parent_to_another_recipient_is_refused`, `test_scrub_keeps_text_without_findings_unchanged`). These changes were made in the private development repository before publication, so the PRs are not linkable; the tests are in the public tree.
tests_documented_added_justification: The policy is stated in the contribution instructions themselves (`CONTRIBUTING.md#tests`).
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Dependencies are PyPI packages installed by pip; Dependabot tracks pip and GitHub Actions updates. The one vendored component, the structural PII detector from presidio-hardened-x402 (ADR-0003), is checked against its upstream by `tests/test_detect.py::test_parity_with_x402` in CI, so an upstream change shows up as a failing test; replacing it with a shared package is planned.
version_semver_justification: URL: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/SEMVER.md` — semantic versioning with the documented 0.x rules (additive changes are minor, patch releases fix bugs and security defects only); the record and result formats are versioned separately (`@1`, `@2`).
version_tags_justification: Releases are tagged `vX.Y.Z` (`v0.7.0`, `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/tags`); the tag is an annotated, SSH-signed tag that GitHub shows as Verified. Versions 0.1.0 to 0.6.0 were never published.
version_tags_signed_justification: The release tag `v0.7.0` is SSH-signed with the organisation release key and shown as Verified on GitHub; `git -c gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile=allowed_signers verify-tag v0.7.0` checks it locally.
version_unique_justification: One version in `pyproject.toml` per release; each release is a `vX.Y.Z` tag and one `CHANGELOG.md` entry; PyPI refuses to reuse a version.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability has arisen in the project or its dependencies; `pip-audit` would fail CI on one.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No known unpatched medium+ vulnerabilities. `pip-audit` runs in CI on every push and PR (`ci.yml`, required check `audit`); Dependabot alerts and security updates are enabled, with no open alerts. The only runtime dependency is `presidio-evidence[crypto]` (bringing `cryptography`).
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerability report has been received or resolved in the last 12 months; no security advisory exists for this repository. `GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities` assigns reporter credit to the security contact.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: URL: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability` — private GitHub Security Advisory ("Security → Report a vulnerability", private vulnerability reporting enabled) or `security@presidio-group.eu`; acknowledgement within 5 business days (`CONTRIBUTING.md#reporting-a-security-vulnerability`).
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received in the last 6 months: no security advisory, draft or published, exists for this repository, which was private until 2026-11-08.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: Intake by private GitHub Security Advisory or `security@presidio-group.eu` (`https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-deident/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability`); acknowledgement within 5 business days (`CONTRIBUTING.md#reporting-a-security-vulnerability`); the security contact triages, coordinates the fix, the advisory and reporter credit (`GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities`); a verification defect ships as a patch release with an advisory (`SEMVER.md`).
